name: APT Balance
summary: Dry-powder bacteria made to cope with the low pH of aquasoil tanks. One sachet holds nitrifying bacteria to clear ammonia and nitrite, the other holds bacteria that break down mulm and plant waste.
bestFor: New aquasoil tanks during cycling, and monthly or after a rescape, filter clean or new livestock.
highlights: Bacteria chosen for low-pH aquasoil tanks
Nitrifying plus waste-digesting cultures
Dry powder, stored at room temperature

specs.Form: Dry powder in two sachets (A and B)
specs.How often: Monthly, and after resets or filter cleans

watchOut: Switch off any UV steriliser for 24 hours after dosing, and keep testing during a cycle.

name: APT Dew
summary: A balanced macro, micro and trace fertiliser in a spray bottle, applied to leaves instead of the water. For aquarium keepers it is most useful during the dry-start method, feeding a carpet while it grows in before the tank is flooded.
bestFor: The dry-start phase of a carpet, and plants growing above the waterline in an open-top tank.
highlights: Foliar spray with macro, micro and trace nutrients
Feeds plants grown out of water
Useful during a dry start
watchOut: It is a spray for leaves out of water, not a fertiliser to dose into the aquarium.

name: APT Feast
summary: A nutrient-rich aquasoil that feeds roots and softens the water. 2HR rates it for a sustained boost of about 12 months, with pH settling around 6.2 to 6.6, and says no substrate booster is needed on top.
bestFor: New planted tanks and soft-water shrimp setups that want a feeding substrate from day one.
highlights: Organic, nutrient-rich aquasoil
Softens water, pH about 6.2 to 6.6
Feeds roots for around a year

specs.Adds nitrate and phosphate: Some N and P from the soil
specs.How often: Once, at setup (about 12 months of nutrients)

watchOut: Like most rich aquasoils it needs a settling-in period; 2HR advises full water changes every other day for the first two weeks in an uncycled tank.

name: APT Fix
summary: A spot treatment for stubborn algae, especially black beard, staghorn and the stringy or fuzzy filamentous types. You dose it straight onto the algae with the flow off, and it biodegrades.
bestFor: Planted tanks with patches of black beard algae or hair algae on hardscape and slow plants.
highlights: Targets BBA and filamentous algae
Applied directly onto the algae
Biodegrades completely

specs.Suits: BBA, hair, string and fuzz algae
specs.Sizes: Starter (100 ml), Standard (300 ml), 200 ml, 500 ml, 600 ml

watchOut: Keep it off mosses and delicate plants (APT FixLite is made for those), and stay under 1 ml per 10 L; 2HR says to do an 80% water change if you go over.

name: APT FixLite
summary: A gentler version of APT Fix for tanks with mosses, liverworts such as riccardia and riccia, vallisneria and other delicate plants that full-strength treatments can knock back.
bestFor: Moss-heavy and delicate-plant tanks that still need to tackle algae.
highlights: Milder algae treatment, gentler on beneficial microbes
Made for tanks with mosses, liverworts and vallisneria
Biodegrades completely

specs.Suits: Tanks with mosses, liverworts and vallisneria

watchOut: Milder does not mean slower (2HR says it often acts faster than APT Fix), so keep circulation and oxygen up after dosing and stay under 1 ml per 10 L.

name: APT Jazz
summary: Slow-release capsules pushed into the substrate that feed roots with nitrogen (mostly ammonium) plus magnesium and traces. 2HR pitches them at reviving tired, older aquasoil, used alongside a liquid fertiliser rather than instead of one.
bestFor: Mature or depleted aquasoil and fine-grained inert substrates, especially around heavy root feeders.
highlights: Slow-release root capsules, one per 4 x 4 cm
Mostly ammoniacal nitrogen, almost no phosphate
Designed to be used with 2HR's liquid fertilisers

specs.Supplies: Nitrogen (mostly ammoniacal), magnesium, iron and traces
specs.Adds nitrate and phosphate: Nitrogen into the substrate, almost no phosphate
specs.Sizes: Mini (9 caps), Small (18 caps), Large (54 caps)

watchOut: Push capsules at least 2.5 cm deep; shallow placement can leak ammonia into the water.

name: APT Pure
summary: A concentrated dechlorinator for water changes. It removes chlorine and chloramine and detoxifies ammonia, nitrite, nitrate and heavy metals, with aloe vera added. One ml treats 60 L.
bestFor: Anyone doing water changes with tap water.
highlights: Removes chlorine and chloramine
Detoxifies ammonia, nitrite, nitrate and heavy metals
1 ml per 60 L, so a bottle lasts

specs.Sizes: Starter (100 ml), Standard (300 ml), 200 ml, 500 ml

watchOut: A garlic or sulphur smell is normal; it comes from the hydrosulfite it is based on.

name: APT Sky
summary: A remineraliser that puts calcium, magnesium and trace minerals back into RO or RODI water without touching KH, pH or NPK. It lets shrimp and hard-water plants do well alongside soft-water plants.
bestFor: Soft-water planted tanks and Caridina shrimp tanks started from RO water.
highlights: Restores GH in RO and RODI water
Does not raise KH or pH
No added nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium

specs.How often: Every water change with RO water
specs.Sizes: Mini (70 g), Small (150 g), Large (800 g)

watchOut: It is for RO or RODI water; adding it to hard tap water will push GH higher than you want.

name: APT Sky Plus
summary: Like APT Sky, it remineralises RO or RODI water without adding NPK, but it also raises KH to about 2 dKH and pH to around 7.2 to 7.6. 2HR notes that level of KH still suits most commercial aquarium plants.
bestFor: RO-water tanks with Neocaridina shrimp or plants that like a little buffering.
highlights: Restores GH in RO and RODI water
Raises KH to about 2 and pH to 7.2 to 7.6
No added nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium

specs.Supplies: Calcium, magnesium, trace minerals plus KH buffer
specs.Effect on KH and pH: Raises KH to about 2, pH to 7.2 to 7.6
specs.How often: Every water change with RO water

watchOut: Caridina such as crystal shrimp usually want KH near zero and pH below 7, so plain APT Sky suits them better.

name: APT Start
summary: A one-off booster for new tanks: a pouch of substrate fertiliser spread under the soil, plus a sachet of dormant starter bacteria poured into the water after filling. It adds ammoniacal nitrogen at the roots and helps the first cycle get going.
bestFor: Brand-new tanks at the build stage, before the substrate goes in, on most aquasoils other than APT Feast.
highlights: Substrate fertiliser plus starter bacteria
Spread under the substrate at setup
Helps a new tank cycle faster

specs.Supplies: Nitrogen, potassium, calcium, magnesium and starter bacteria
specs.Adds nitrate and phosphate: Nitrogen (mostly ammoniacal) into the substrate, no phosphate
specs.Form: Pouch of substrate fertiliser plus bacteria sachet
specs.Sizes: 45 g pouch (about 60 L or a 60 x 30 cm footprint)

watchOut: It is a setup product that releases some ammonia while cycling, and it does not replace ongoing fertiliser dosing.

name: APT1
summary: APT3's formula with the nitrate and phosphate taken out. It is for tanks where fish food and waste already supply plenty of nitrogen and phosphorus, and 2HR also suggests it for the first one to three months of any new tank.
bestFor: New tanks in their first few months, and well-stocked tanks where nitrate already reads high.
highlights: Potassium, magnesium, iron and traces
Zero added nitrate and phosphate
2HR's pick for the first months of a new tank

specs.Sizes: Starter (100 ml), Standard (300 ml), 200 ml, 500 ml, 600 ml, 1000 ml

watchOut: In a lightly stocked tank plants can run short of nitrogen and phosphorus on APT1 alone.

name: APT3
summary: A liquid fertiliser that covers macro, micro and trace nutrients in one bottle, so a single daily dose replaces mixing separate products. The standard dose is set for CO2 tanks, and 2HR's dosage calculator scales it down for tanks without CO2 or full of slow growers.
bestFor: Planted tanks with a normal fish load, with or without CO2, that want one simple fertiliser.
highlights: Macro, micro and trace nutrients in one bottle
One product to dose, no dry salts to mix
2HR's balanced ratio aimed at strong growth and good red colour

specs.Supplies: Macro (N, P, K), magnesium, iron and traces
specs.Suits: CO2 and non-CO2 tanks, normal fish load
specs.Sizes: Starter (100 ml), Standard (300 ml), 200 ml, 500 ml, 600 ml, 1000 ml

watchOut: If nitrate keeps building up because of a heavy fish load, APT1 (no nitrate or phosphate) is the better fit.

name: APTe (APT EI)
summary: A ready-mixed take on the Estimative Index method: generous, non-limiting doses of every nutrient, dosed daily. EI is traditionally paired with a big weekly water change to reset levels, and this gives you the approach without weighing out dry salts.
bestFor: Fast-growing, high-light CO2 tanks where you do a large water change every week.
highlights: Based on the Estimative Index dosing method
Generous, non-limiting nutrient levels
No dry salts to weigh or mix

specs.Supplies: Macro, micro and trace at EI levels
specs.How often: Daily (EI usually pairs this with a large weekly water change)

watchOut: EI normally relies on large weekly water changes to stop nutrients building up, so it asks more upkeep than a leaner fertiliser.

name: Bottom Plus
summary: Slow-release root sticks pushed into the substrate next to root-feeding plants, topping up the nitrogen and iron that run out of a substrate over time. Made mostly from the same natural soil as ADA Aqua Soil, they break down completely.
bestFor: Swords, crypts, vallisneria and other root feeders, especially in older or inert substrate.
highlights: Nitrogen and iron at the roots
Made from Aqua Soil type soil, breaks down fully
Successor to ADA's Iron Bottom and Multi Bottom

specs.Adds nitrate and phosphate: Nitrogen into the substrate, phosphate not stated
specs.How often: Follow the label (retailers quote 1 to 6 months)

watchOut: Push sticks fully under the substrate; exposed sticks can leach nutrients and feed algae.

name: ECA Plus
summary: An iron and magnesium additive, with the iron in the ferrous form plants take up easily and organic acids to help absorption. ADA says it both prevents and treats chlorosis, where new leaves come in pale or yellow, and brings out green and red colour.
bestFor: Tanks where new growth has gone pale or yellow, or red plants that need more iron.
highlights: Ferrous iron plus magnesium
Organic acids to aid uptake
Prevents and treats pale new growth

specs.How often: Follow the label; daily for a short spell when correcting chlorosis

watchOut: Too much iron can feed algae, so dose by the drop and do not stack it on top of heavy iron dosing from other products.

name: Green Brighty Iron
summary: A liquid iron supplement from ADA's Green Brighty range, for vigorously growing plants that use a lot of iron. ADA intends it for daily dosing, and it is normally used as part of the Green Brighty system with the other bottles.
bestFor: Fast-growing and red plants showing pale new growth from low iron.
highlights: Supplies iron
Part of ADA's modular Green Brighty range
Pump bottle for measured doses
watchOut: Pale new leaves are not always iron. Check the deficiency guide first so you do not overdose one nutrient.

name: Green Brighty Mineral
summary: ADA's trace element supplement, supplying the minor nutrients plants need for healthy new buds and pigment. It is the trace part of the Green Brighty system.
bestFor: Planted tanks on ADA's Green Brighty system that need trace elements topped up.
highlights: Supplies trace elements
Supports new bud growth and colour
Pump bottle for measured doses

name: Green Brighty Neutral K
summary: A potassium supplement that does not raise pH or KH. ADA pitches it for plants that dislike high pH and KH, and it is the neutral alternative to Brighty K, which is alkaline and adds buffering.
bestFor: Soft-water plants, and tanks where potassium is short but pH and KH should not climb.
highlights: Supplies potassium
Does not raise pH or KH
Neutral alternative to the alkaline Brighty K

specs.Suits: Soft-water plants, tanks that should not gain KH

name: Green Brighty Nitrogen
summary: ADA's nitrogen supplement, dosed daily to keep leaf colour strong and growth steady in tanks where plants use up nitrogen faster than fish produce it.
bestFor: Heavily planted, lightly stocked tanks where older leaves yellow from low nitrogen.
highlights: Supplies nitrogen
Supports leaf colour and growth
Pump bottle for measured doses
watchOut: Skip or reduce it in well-stocked tanks where nitrate already reads high.

name: Green Gain Plus
summary: A plant supplement based on seaweed-derived plant hormones, trace elements and amino acids, with boron for new buds. ADA pitches it for easing stress after pruning or when conditions dip, and for pushing new shoots.
bestFor: Freshly trimmed or newly planted tanks where you want faster regrowth of new shoots.
highlights: Seaweed-derived plant hormones
Trace elements, amino acids and boron
Helps plants recover after trimming

specs.Supplies: Plant hormones, amino acids, trace, boron
specs.How often: For a few days after trimming (follow the label)

watchOut: It supports growth rather than supplying the main nutrients, so use it with a regular fertiliser.
